summary: AI frame-sourcing now honors the capture mode (standalone / siphon / auto) — previously these were config-only and the monitor always did a standalone RTSP grab. The recorder ffmpeg gains an optional MJPEG tee (a second downscaled output at SiphonFPS) into an in-memory latest-frame buffer (Manager.LatestFrame), so the detector can read decoded frames off the recording stream without a second decode. New services.DetectionSource resolves the frame by mode: standalone = one-shot RTSP grab; siphon = the recorder's latest decoded frame; auto = a fresh siphon frame (within the stale limit) else a standalone grab. Critically, ALL modes are pinned to the RECORDING stream when a camera records (so auto never alternates between streams and zone/line geometry stays stable); cameras with no recording config fall back to the live stream. New GET /api/vision/cameras/{id}/frame returns the exact frame the detector samples, and the rule-editor zone/line preview now draws on that — so what you draw on is provably what gets detected, even when the recording and live streams differ.
compatibility: Backward compatible. The siphon tee only runs in siphon/auto modes (standalone pays no extra recorder decode). Detection moving to the recording stream is matched by the preview, so existing rules stay aligned; switching a camera's recording stream to a different field-of-view may require redrawing zones/lines. The detection-frame preview is a periodic still (not live video) and does not affect detection performance.
